raw_segments.text: Two gates the silent house of sleep adorn, Of polished ivory this, that of transparent
horn, True visions through transparent horn arise,
Throw polished ivory past deluding lies, Of various things discoursing as he passed,
And Cayce's hither bends his steps at last. Then, throw the gate of ivory, he dismissed
His valiant offspring and divining guest. Straight to the ships Aeneas took his way,
Embarked his men, and skimmed along the sea, Still coasting, till he gained Cajeta's
way. At length on oozy ground his galleys more,
Their heads are turned to sea, their sterns to shore.
